text: Why is putting an access point on channel 3 to 'avoid' neighbours on 1 and 6 worse than sharing channel 1 with them?
choices: Channel 3 is not permitted in most regions
Two networks on the same channel can hear each other and take turns under CSMA/CA; partially overlapping networks cannot decode each other, so neither defers and both corrupt each other's frames
explanation: Co-channel interference costs throughput; adjacent-channel interference costs the link. This is one of the most common well-intentioned mistakes in wireless deployment.
